cells.tense: You are holding the spark right now, and it is yours to hold.
cells.ask: When the ground shifts, write the first thing you actually think and keep that page. Then go do one ordinary thing you said you would. What the fire is for gets chosen again tomorrow.
cells.core:
There's something building in you, and you're not faking it. People come awake around you — not because you're performing, but because what you're carrying is real and it moves. You start things before they're polished. When a structure that doesn't fit cracks open, you don't mourn it; you see daylight.

You can cut to what's true, so what's new is letting that set the direction instead of the mood. A morning that doesn't run hot is not a problem to fix. The part you own is doing what you said you'd do when the spark stops being fun and turns into a job. That's what keeps the fire yours.
cells.sheetLine: The spark is real. What you do next is the part you own.
cells.verb: starting something alive before you know where it leads
cells.place: where a structure that was never true comes apart

cells.tense: You are living in a version of this that has not arrived, bracing against it instead of standing where you are.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're set to launch this week and describe it to one person without selling it. Sit through the pause after. If it dies in that quiet, let it die there.
cells.core:
You're already announcing what hasn't happened. The fire is real, but it's been running ahead of itself — talking past the room, lighting up plans nobody's asked for yet, rehearsing the version of the story where it all worked. When a false structure gives way for you, you'll be mid-sentence you can't finish, and it will feel like being caught rather than freed.

None of it is fake. It's just ahead of what's actually been built, and your own ear knows the difference. What's underneath is a recognition that arrives whole and doesn't need a slide deck. When you stop pushing, the thing is there in the room with you — and you find out what you actually have by not overproducing it.

cells.tense: You are at a door you already walked through, waiting for someone to let you back in.
cells.ask: Do a small physical thing first — make the bed, water the plant, chop the onion — before you try to feel inspired. Hands first, feeling after. Keep it that ordinary.
cells.core:
The light went out somewhere, and you went quiet with it. You know how to be lit, but the habit of letting anyone see it is gone, and waiting for the spark to come back on its own hasn't worked. Meanwhile the thing you're meant to do sits there untouched.

You've been treating care as something you earn by getting it right, which is why tending anything feels like work. What's dry isn't the spark; it's the ground it needs, and ground gets made by hand. Make one ordinary thing go well — a plant, a meal, a room — and let the pleasure count for itself. It doesn't have to prove anything. Doing it is the whole point, and it starts small enough that being tired doesn't stop you.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing grows until you tend something actual.

cells.tense: You are writing the thing you keep calling the room's, and your hand is already on the pen.
cells.ask: Say plainly, to one person, that the last good call came from your judgment. One sentence, no pitch, no apology, no follow-up. It stands on its own.
cells.core:
You're already starting the fire — and then talking about it like it caught on its own. You take the step and describe the step as the group's idea. People feel you holding the room steady, and you'll call that luck, or the team, or just showing up. When the old structure gives way, you'll be the one with footing while it comes down, and you won't put your name on it.

That holding doesn't need permission and doesn't need announcing. It's simply that you keep your balance while things fall apart, and you've been generous with it to the point of disappearing into it. One honest sentence, to one person, brings you back to the front of your own life — and nothing bigger is required.
cells.sheetLine: You did it. The only missing piece is saying so.

attempts.check: The record doesn't say the collapse of false structure is already underway in someone's present, only that when it comes it lands as liberation — so a reading that tells them what is falling, or that it has fallen and they missed it, is reaching further than the card can carry. A reader could fairly say 'I don't know what you mean by false structure in my life,' and the cells still need to leave them something usable — a fire that can be attended to, or held back — which they do, because the ask never depends on my having the collapse right. The sentence that serves me more than them is anything that makes suddenness sound like a promise I can deliver.

attempts.check: The record gives me a spark that's real and a clearing that arrives as liberation — it does not tell me what in this person's life is false, what has already fallen, or what they feel about it, so the cells stay about one capacity doing its work, never about their history or their worth. A reader could fairly say 'I don't recognise this at all,' and the asks still hold, because each one is a move they can make whether or not my read lands — nothing is promised and nothing is diagnosed. The sentence that would serve me more than them is anything that turns the clearing into an event I'm announcing, as if I could say when it comes or what it costs.
